subject: Priority commitment exception request – Elmwood Platforms
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Elmwood: request for prioritized availability commitment (context + ask)

Team — quick context: Elmwood (priority expansion account) is asking for an availability/latency commitment above our standard platform terms as part of a renewal negotiation. They want a written operational commitment that reads roughly: 99.99% monthly availability and p95 inference latency <= 70ms for their production traffic in us-west region, with a runbook and 15‑min pager for Sev1.

They've flagged that their go‑live window for a new feature is late Sep and want this included in the contract amendments. HubSpot shows this as an expansion deal (RDW-ELM-2026-001) with ARR upside. I attached their Q2 traffic profile (elmwood_traffic_profile_q2.pdf) and a rough draft of the proposed terms (proposed-availability-terms-draft.docx).

Asks:
- Marissa: sanity-check product feasibility and required roadmap or config changes (can we meet p95 70ms for their expected QPS with current routing/batching knobs?)
- Markus: estimate runbook / infra ops changes and any capacity reservation needed (dedicated pool? burst policy?).
- Ben / Jasmine: highlight contract risk and procurement path if we need a custom SLO and additional SLAs.

Goal: get internal alignment this week so I can give Elmwood a clear yes/no and an ask list for the commercial counter.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Elmwood: request for prioritized availability commitment (context + ask)

Avery — thanks for the context and attachments. Initial thoughts:

- Latency: p95 <=70ms is reachable in the hosted us-west cluster for many seq-length-512 workloads today, but it depends on their exact model variant, token mix, and concurrency profile. The traffic profile helps; their median seq len and request-size distribution look favorable.
- Availability: 99.99% is a significant uptick from our standard 99.9% for shared-hosted. To guarantee that, we'd need either a dedicated capacity commitment (Reserved pool) or an explicit multi-region failover with priority routing.

Questions for Avery / Ben:
1) Are they expecting this on Hosted (no infra changes) or are they open to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) as part of the commercial ask?
2) What SLA credit/penalty model are they proposing — or is this a verbal ask to be formalized?

Operationally, if we move forward:
- We'll need a short MOP (runbook) and a documented MoS (modes of service) for failover and cache warming.
- We'll also need to define acceptable maintenance windows and notification commitments.

I can scope what work looks like and a high-level ETA for deliverables if we decide to offer an exception. Tentative: 3–4 weeks for runbook + testing if we use an existing dedicated pool, longer if we need new infra.

—Marissa
Product Lead, Redwood Console
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16 08:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Elmwood: request for prioritized availability commitment (context + ask)

Avery / Marissa — read the traffic profile. Short answer: technically feasible, with caveats. Notes: 

- Dedicated pool recommended: to get deterministic p95 latency and 99.99% availability we should put Elmwood on a reserved pool sized to their 95th percentile QPS + 20% buffer. Shared pools introduce noisy neighbor risk.
- Capacity lead time: depending on GPU type we may need 10–21 days to provision and validate (autoscaling config and warm caches).
- Failover: multi-AZ routing within us-west is doable; cross-region failover (us-west -> us-east) adds complexity and will require replication of model weights and KV cache priming strategy.

Requested deliverables from Eng:
- Capacity sizing spreadsheet (I started one: mop-appendix-elmwood.xlsx)
- Runbook draft for incident response and planned maintenance
- Performance test plan against the Elmwood traffic profile

If sales wants to promise the 99.99% SLA, we should make it contingent on Dedicated or explicit burst-reserve commit in the contract. I can slice effort into a minimal viable commitment that reduces time-to-green.

-Markus
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17 10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Elmwood: request for prioritized availability commitment (context + ask)

Avery — appreciate the heads-up. A few commercial and procurement items to consider:

- Price: guaranteeing 99.99% and dedicated capacity should be priced as a reserved capacity contract (monthly commit) with a term (12–24 months). We should build a premium into the billing for the reservation and the prioritized support (15‑min pager rotation).
- Credits model: define clear SLA triggers and credit calculation (e.g., percentage of monthly committed fee prorated by minutes of downtime). Avoid open-ended penalty language.
- Legal: Jasmine, please weigh in on indemnification and force majeure carveouts; we should avoid hard availability penalties that we can't operationally support.

Avery, if Elmwood is a high strategic seller with clear ARR upside, this can be done quickly — but we need a commercial skeleton to present with the Yes. If no, we push for Dedicated + commercial uplift as the path forward.

-Ben
Head of Sales Ops
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-18 16:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Elmwood: request for prioritized availability commitment (context + ask)

Thanks all — I reviewed the draft terms. Legal position and suggested contractual guardrails: 

1) Make the commitment conditional: any availability SLA > 99.95% requires Dedicated capacity or an approved architecture diagram that shows redundancy and failover exercises.
2) Cap credits: SLA credits should be capped at a percentage of the monthly fee (e.g., up to 25%) to limit open exposure.
3) Exclude third-party cloud outages and customer-side misconfigurations from availability calculations; define measurement method (synthetic probes + customer telemetry).
4) Require a joint runbook and quarterly reliability review with Elmwood; include a remediation timeline for repeated breaches rather than automatic termination rights.

Next steps: if Sales wants to propose this path to Elmwood, I'll prepare a redlineable amendment (we'll need procurement input for billing cadence). Also recommend we run a short failover test during staging to validate multi-AZ behavior before contract signature.

—Jasmine
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
